sources.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (University of California, Davis; revised 6/18/2014, 242 pp.)
sources.locator: Chapters 2 (2.1-2.7), 3 (3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 3.9, 3.10) and 4 (4.1-4.12) read completely over the named sections, together with Chapter 7 (7.1-7.5) inspected for row dispositions; printed page numbers are the text's own chapter numbering (Ch. 2 pp. 19-46, Ch. 3 pp. 47-90, Ch. 4 pp. 91-126, Ch. 7 pp. 211-230)

contents.name: Ch. 2.1 Mean value theorem for harmonic functions and Ch. 2.2 derivative estimates and analyticity
contents.support: The interior derivative estimates and mean-value machinery used to make the spherical-harmonic partial-sum derivatives converge uniformly on smaller balls; the pair consumes the published library form thm-interior-derivative-estimates-for-harmonic-functions, and this source confirms its standard statement C_{n,alpha} r^{-n-|alpha|} integral bound.

contents.name: Ch. 2.5 Green's identities
contents.support: The ball Green identity used to prove orthogonality of homogeneous harmonic polynomials of distinct degrees; the pair uses the published library forms cor-first/second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain, whose statements match this source's identities with outward normals.

contents.name: Ch. 2.6 Fundamental solution and Ch. 2.7 Newtonian potential
contents.support: The computation -Delta(1/(4 pi |x|)) = delta_0 off the pole and the resulting Newtonian potential integral; the pair states the exact distributional identity as its published supplier thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally and upgrades smoothness of compactly supported smooth data by parameter differentiation.

contents.name: Ch. 3.1 Weak derivatives, Ch. 3.3 Distributions and Ch. 3.5 Sobolev spaces
contents.support: The definitions of weak derivatives, L^2-based Sobolev spaces and their norm used by the pair's H^1 and H_0^1 statements; the pair consumes the published library definitions def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm and def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure, whose conventions coincide with this source's.

contents.name: Ch. 3.6 Approximation of Sobolev functions
contents.support: Density of smooth functions in Sobolev spaces, which the recorded chart-transfer argument invokes through the published density theorem thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains; this source's approximation theorem corroborates the standard statement.

contents.name: Ch. 3.9 Boundary values of Sobolev functions
contents.support: The trace inequality and boundary values in W^{1,p}; the pair uses the published trace chain (thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p, thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace, thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero) and this source confirms the standard bounded-trace statement.

contents.name: Ch. 3.10 Compactness results
contents.support: The Rellich-Kondrachov compactness statement for bounded domains; the pair records an elementary cube-averaging proof of the compact H^1 into L^2 inclusion in place of the citation, and this source confirms the standard result.

contents.name: Ch. 4.1 Weak formulation of the Dirichlet problem, Ch. 4.3 the space H^{-1}, Ch. 4.5 existence of weak solutions
contents.support: The weak formulation of -div(eps grad u)=rho and existence by coercivity; the pair's lift lemma states the same weak problem with a prescribed lift G and consumes the published Sobolev definitions, matching this source's formulation.

contents.name: Ch. 4.4 The Poincare inequality for H_0^1 (Theorem 4.9, Eq. 4.11)
contents.support: For Omega bounded in some direction, the integral of u^2 over Omega is at most C times the integral of |Du|^2 for u in H_0^1(Omega), proved from the one-variable fundamental theorem and Cauchy-Schwarz; the pair's recorded box-line proof is the same argument with explicit constant 2L.

contents.name: Ch. 4.7 The Lax-Milgram theorem and general elliptic PDEs (Theorem 4.20)
contents.support: Unique solvability a(u,v)=f(v) for a bounded coercive bilinear form on a Hilbert space; the pair instead proves the symmetric case by direct minimisation of J(v)=a(v,v)/2-l(v) with Countable Choice, so no citation is used; this source confirms the statement's hypotheses (coercivity C1||u||^2 <= a(u,u), boundedness).

contents.name: Ch. 4.8 Compactness of the resolvent, Ch. 4.9 The Fredholm alternative, Ch. 4.10 The spectrum of a self-adjoint elliptic operator
contents.support: Compactness of the resolvent of a uniformly elliptic operator, the Fredholm alternative and the discrete spectrum with finite multiplicities; the pair's PEC cavity closure obtains the same structure on the curl form and consumes the published thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators.

contents.name: Ch. 4.11 Interior regularity, Ch. 4.12 Boundary regularity
contents.support: Interior and boundary H^2 and higher regularity for uniformly elliptic divergence-form equations with smooth data; the pair's difference-quotient/normal-recovery induction is a fully expanded form of this argument and uses the published Sobolev extension and Fourier-characterisation theorems for the classical representative.

contents.name: Ch. 7.1-7.5 The wave equation: weak solutions, existence, uniqueness
contents.reason: The weak-solution existence theory for the wave equation belongs to the later EM pages em-wave-equation-prerequisites and em-causal-wave-kernel-prerequisites, which own the corresponding items; no item scaffolded in batch 16 asserts a weak wave solution, and this pair only needs the spherical mean identity, which is scaffolded locally with its own suppliers.

sources.title: S. Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155: distributions, elliptic regularity, and applications to PDEs (MIT, Fall 2022, 263 pp.)
sources.locator: Chapters 1 (1.1.1), 9 (9.1-9.2), 11-12 (12.1-12.2), 15 (15.1-15.3) and 16 (16.1) read over the named sections, with Chapters 10 and 17 inspected for the decline rows; printed page numbers are the text's own table-of-contents numbering (Ch. 1 pp. 9-26, Ch. 9 pp. 97-106, Ch. 12 pp. 139-154, Ch. 15 pp. 199-216, Ch. 16 pp. 217-230)

contents.name: Ch. 1.1.1 Solving Poisson's equation and Ch. 9.1 Fundamental solutions
contents.support: The computation that the Coulomb potential E(x) = -1/(4 pi |x|) satisfies Delta E = delta_0 distributionally, with the distributional justification of differentiating under the integral sign and the weak-versus-classical discussion; this is exactly the identity and smoothness upgrade recorded in the pair's smooth-Newtonian lemma and its outgoing fundamental-solution supplier.

contents.name: Ch. 12.1 Sobolev spaces and Ch. 12.2 Elliptic regularity II
contents.support: The Fourier/Bessel-potential definition of Sobolev spaces, their completeness and the elliptic regularity estimate; the pair's H^1/H_0^1 statements and its Sobolev supplier set match these conventions, and the Fredholm/regularity structure is used by the interior-regularity lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 9.2 Elliptic regularity I
contents.support: Smoothness of solutions of elliptic equations with smooth data (interior regularity before Sobolev scales); the pair's complete induction gives the same conclusion on bounded smooth domains and across smooth interfaces with explicit hypotheses.

contents.name: Ch. 15.1 Elliptic regularity in Sobolev spaces, Ch. 15.2 Compact embedding in Sobolev spaces (Rellich-Kondrachov, Theorems 15.8 and 15.10), Ch. 15.3 Fredholm theory
contents.support: The elliptic estimate u in H^{s+m}_loc whenever Pu in H^s_loc, compact embeddings on compact manifolds and the Fredholm mapping property; the pair's smooth-domain regularity theorem and the PEC cavity Fredholm step use exactly this structure, with the pair supplying its own elementary compactness proof.

contents.name: Ch. 16.1 Spectral theorem for self-adjoint elliptic operators
contents.support: Discreteness of the spectrum of a self-adjoint elliptic operator with finite multiplicities; the pair's curl-form spectral closure obtains the nonnegative eigenvalues with finite multiplicity and the retained zero eigenspace, consuming the published compact self-adjoint spectral theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 10 Application to the wave equation and Ch. 11-12 Fourier transform on distributions
contents.reason: The distributional wave-equation solution theory and the general Fourier-transform-on-distributions machinery are owned by the later EM wave pages and by the imported Fourier suppliers; no item of this pair needs the pullback construction, and the pair's finite-subtraction lemma uses the local contour argument instead.

contents.name: Ch. 17 Differential forms and Hodge theory
contents.reason: The Hodge decomposition on manifolds and the de Rham complex have no consumer in this pair: the PEC cavity closure uses the abstract compact self-adjoint Hilbert-space spectral theorem (already an imported published supplier), not a manifold Hodge theorem.

contents.name: Sec. 18.12, Eq. 18.12.4: the Legendre generating function (1-2xz+z^2)^{-1/2} = sum_{n>=0} P_n(x) z^n (A&S 22.9.3)
contents.support: The generating-function identity for the Legendre polynomials. The pair does not cite it: its recorded proof re-derives the identity by integrating the geometric series in the defining theta-integral and using the tangent substitution, so the source is corroborative of the statement and the analytic branch at q=0.

sources.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 14 (Legendre and Related Functions), Sec. 14.30 Spherical and Spheroidal Harmonics
sources.locator: Sec. 14.30 complete with the Addition Theorem subsection 14.30(iii), in particular Eq. 14.30.9

contents.name: Sec. 14.30(iii), Eq. 14.30.9: the addition theorem P_l(cos(theta1)cos(theta2)+sin(theta1)sin(theta2)cos(phi1-phi2)) = (4 pi/(2l+1)) sum_{m=-l}^{l} conj(Y_{l,m}(theta1,phi1)) Y_{l,m}(theta2,phi2)
contents.support: The addition theorem in normalized complex spherical harmonics; the pair states the equivalent real-orthonormal-basis form sum_m Y_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n') = (2l+1)/(4 pi) P_l(n.n') and re-proves it from rotation invariance and the zonal polynomial, so this source is corroborative of the normalization and the exact constant.

sources.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10 (Bessel Functions), Sec. 10.47 Standard Solutions of the Spherical Bessel Equation and Sec. 10.50 Wronskians and Cross-Products
sources.locator: Sec. 10.47 complete (Eqs. 10.47.1-10.47.9, in particular 10.47.3-10.47.5 for the standard solutions and the third-kind spherical Bessel functions), with Sec. 10.50 checked for the Wronskian identities

contents.name: Sec. 10.47(i)-(ii): the spherical Bessel differential equation z^2 w''+2zw'+(z^2-n(n+1))w=0 and its standard solutions, Eq. 10.47.5 expressing the spherical Bessel functions of the third kind through Hankel functions
contents.support: The radial equation solved by the pair's explicit outgoing functions h_l(z) and the identification of the two independent solution families with the incoming/outgoing third-kind functions; the pair proves the ODE, nonvanishing and exact coefficient bounds directly from the explicit factorial polynomials rather than citing the special-function theory.

contents.name: Sec. 10.50: Wronskian relations among the spherical Bessel functions
contents.support: The nonvanishing Wronskian of the two independent radial solutions, which the pair's F2 use invokes to show that the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of h_l and its incoming partner; the pair re-derives the needed identity Im(conj(h)h') = z^{-2}.
